args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks after deploy to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback rolled out and verified in us-east, us-west, eu-west. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **What went wrong:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 18%. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. A status check afterwards shows the service healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It says why we rolled back, what we rolled back to, that it went out in all regions, and that the v2.3.1 bug needs looking into before anyone redeploys it. I wrote it just before that last status check, so it doesn't include the new error rate.

v2.3.1 shouldn't go back out until it's fixed. It has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it would need change-manager approval anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
